It checks that files used in Linux (main_controller.py, sim_worlds' make_mission.py, docker/Dockerfile, launcher.sh, check_host.sh) check out with LF, that the .bat launchers keep CRLF, that pictures, PDFs and model weights are never converted, that no shell script is committed with CRLF, and that every committed '#!' script stored with LF also gets LF on checkout.
mod:simulation/docker/test/test_line_end.how_it_fits: Protects Windows clones: with CRLF line ends a shell script or a '#!/usr/bin/env python3' line fails in Linux, because the hidden carriage return becomes part of the command. check_host.sh --fix-line-endings and check_host.ps1 report and repair the same problem on a teammate's PC. New on 2026-10-31.

pkg:docker.explain: The recipe for the team's Docker images (Dockerfile with three targets: dev, sitl, sim), the compose files that run the simulator as two containers wired like the real drone (compose.sim.yml plus add-ons for WSLg, a Linux desktop, /dev/dri graphics and NVIDIA GPUs), and the pip pin lists the images (and the native setup) install.
pkg:docker.how_it_fits: The 'dev' image mirrors the Jetson's software (Ubuntu 22.04, ROS 2 Humble, MAVROS, the Python ML stack) and is the VS Code dev container everyone uses; 'sitl' adds ArduCopter SITL; 'sim' adds Gazebo Harmonic and everything the simulator needs. simulation/docker/build_images.sh builds them; compose_up.sh / compose_down.sh run and stop compose.sim.yml. AGENTS.md (2026-10-24): 'dev' is used; the compose files and the 'sim' additions are work in progress. setup/01_install_humble.sh reads the same requirements files.

mod:docker/Dockerfile.explain: One Dockerfile, three images (Docker builds only the target you ask for). 'dev' (from ros:humble-ros-base-jammy): build tools, ROS packages the workspace uses, MAVROS 2.14.0 from the frozen ROS snapshot 2026-08-07, mavlink-routerd built from commit 2362c620f483, ONNX Runtime 1.22.0 for C++, the pip packages (CPU PyTorch 2.8.0 by default), ping and ip, and a user 'ubuntu' with password-free sudo. 'sitl' adds ArduCopter SITL built from tag Copter-4.6.3 in /opt/ardupilot. 'sim' (amd64 only) adds Gazebo Harmonic + ros_gz, the ArduPilot Gazebo plugin at a pinned commit in /opt/ardupilot_gazebo, xacro, RViz, PyQt5, the Gazebo Python bindings, Mesa (with the d3d12 driver for WSLg) and GStreamer, and sets ARDUPILOT_SITL_BIN, ARDUPILOT_GAZEBO_DIR and the GZ_SIM_* paths.
mod:docker/Dockerfile.how_it_fits: Every version is an ARG at the top (BUILD_JOBS limits parallel compiles, default 4). The repo is never copied in: it is mounted at run time and ros2_ws is built inside the container, so code changes need no image rebuild. sim_bringup's sim_paths.py looks in /opt/ardupilot and /opt/ardupilot_gazebo as its fallback places. Two 2026-10-31 notes in the file: 'useradd -l' avoids a huge lastlog file with very large user ids, and USERNAME is repeated in the sitl and sim stages so Docker's old builder does not make those images run as root.

mod:docker/compose.sim.yml.explain: Runs the whole digital twin in Docker as TWO containers on a copy of the drone's network 'astra_net' (192.168.144.0/24, gateway .1): 'sim' (image astra-sim, address 192.168.144.25 = the real SIYI camera) runs simulation/docker/container_sim.sh, and 'jetson' (image astra-dev, address 192.168.144.100 = the real Jetson's eth0) runs container_jetson.sh. Both mount the same repo and the host data folder (~/.astra_docker as /home/ubuntu/.astra_sim), use 'ipc: host', ROS_DOMAIN_ID 0 and ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY 0, and keep their own colcon builds in fixed-name volumes (astra_sim_ws_*, astra_jetson_ws_*) plus astra_gz_fuel for 3D models.
mod:docker/compose.sim.yml.how_it_fits: This file alone is headless (no windows, no graphics card); compose_up.sh adds compose.wslg.yml, compose.linux.yml, compose.dri.yml and compose.gpu.yml as needed and fills its ${ASTRA_*} settings from its options. 'pull_policy: never' keeps Docker from asking Docker Hub for images that are only built locally. MAVProxy in 'sim' sends MAVLink to 192.168.144.100:14552, where launcher.sh's MAVROS listens; the SIYI SDK and HTTP media traffic flows the other way to .25. Stop grace periods: 45 s for 'sim' (score report), 30 s for 'jetson'. Needs Docker Compose 2.20 or newer.

mod:docker/compose.wslg.yml.explain: Add-on for compose.sim.yml on WINDOWS (Docker inside WSL2): hands WSLg's X11 and Wayland sockets (/tmp/.X11-unix, /mnt/wslg) to both containers, so their windows appear on the Windows desktop, and gives them WSL2's door to the Windows graphics driver (/dev/dxg) plus the DirectX/CUDA libraries in /usr/lib/wsl/lib, so Mesa's d3d12 driver draws Gazebo and RViz on the real graphics card (GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12, MESA_D3D12_DEFAULT_ADAPTER_NAME default NVIDIA).
mod:docker/compose.wslg.yml.how_it_fits: compose_up.sh adds it by itself inside WSL whenever /mnt/wslg and /dev/dxg exist (also when headless, so Gazebo's camera still renders on the card). Only for WSL2; a normal Linux PC uses compose.linux.yml instead.

mod:docker/compose.linux.yml.explain: Add-on for compose.sim.yml on a LINUX DESKTOP: hands the desktop's X11 socket folder /tmp/.X11-unix and $DISPLAY to both containers (plus a private Qt runtime folder /tmp/runtime-ubuntu and QT_X11_NO_MITSHM=1), so Gazebo, RViz and the demo panel open on your screen; it also works on Ubuntu's Wayland desktop through XWayland.
mod:docker/compose.linux.yml.how_it_fits: compose_up.sh adds it on Linux when the display mode is x11 and runs 'xhost +SI:localuser:<you>' (astra_x11_allow), which only works when the images were built with your user id. For 3D on the graphics hardware add compose.dri.yml or compose.gpu.yml; without either Mesa draws on the processor (slower).

mod:docker/compose.dri.yml.explain: Add-on for compose.sim.yml on a Linux PC: gives both containers /dev/dri (the 'render nodes' of Intel, AMD and some NVIDIA graphics) and adds their user to the group that owns /dev/dri/renderD128 (ASTRA_RENDER_GID, default 'video'), so Gazebo and RViz draw on the graphics hardware through Mesa instead of the processor.
mod:docker/compose.dri.yml.how_it_fits: A separate file because Docker refuses to start a container whose device is missing (WSL2 and virtual machines have no /dev/dri). compose_up.sh adds it when /dev/dri exists outside WSL and reads the group id for ASTRA_RENDER_GID.

mod:docker/compose.gpu.yml.explain: Add-on for compose.sim.yml: asks Docker for all NVIDIA cards for both containers (a 'deploy' device reservation, the same as --gpus all) with NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all (CUDA, nvidia-smi, OpenGL/Vulkan, video), so the team's detector (new_od: YOLO + SAHI on PyTorch, about 10x faster on the card) uses CUDA and, on Linux, Gazebo and RViz draw on the card.
mod:docker/compose.gpu.yml.how_it_fits: Separate because Docker refuses to start a container that asks for a GPU on a PC without an NVIDIA card or without the NVIDIA Container Toolkit; compose_up.sh adds it only when 'docker info' lists the 'nvidia' runtime (never with --no-gpu). PyTorch uses CUDA only when build_images.sh built CUDA PyTorch (--torch cuda, its default on a PC with an NVIDIA card).

mod:docker/requirements-dev.txt.explain: Pip packages every dev image gets, pinned to what the Jetson had in its pip --user folder on 2026-10-10: pymavlink 2.4.49, MAVProxy 1.8.74, pynmeagps 1.1.5, py-spy 0.4.2 and numpy 1.26.4 (kept below 2 so MAVProxy cannot pull numpy 2, which breaks cv_bridge), plus ruff for development only.
mod:docker/requirements-dev.txt.how_it_fits: Installed by docker/Dockerfile ('dev' stage) and by setup/01_install_humble.sh for the native simulator. Part of the fingerprint that build_images.sh stores in each image (org.astra.inputs).

mod:docker/requirements-ml.txt.explain: The Python machine-learning packages of the dev image, the same versions as requirements_jetson.txt: numpy 1.26.4, opencv-python 4.10.0.84, ultralytics 8.4.75, sahi 0.11.36 and watchdog 6.0.0. torch and torchvision are installed separately (they come from PyTorch's own index). numpy must stay below 2 because ROS Humble's cv_bridge is built against numpy 1.x.
mod:docker/requirements-ml.txt.how_it_fits: Installed by docker/Dockerfile when WITH_PY_ML=true (the default) and by setup/01_install_humble.sh. These are what the team's detector new_od (YOLO + SAHI) and its photo-folder watcher need. Part of the image fingerprint (org.astra.inputs).

pkg:simulation/windows.explain: The Windows side of the simulator: five double-click .bat launchers that run the simulator scripts inside the Ubuntu-22.04 WSL distro (Rebuild, Start Search Demo, Start for Mission Planner, Start Over, Stop Simulation), two PowerShell helpers for the Mission Planner plugin (install_mp_plugin.ps1, check_mp_plugin.ps1), and the plugin itself (mission_planner_plugin/astra_gcs.cs).
pkg:simulation/windows.how_it_fits: They let a teammate use the twin without typing Linux commands. Each .bat runs 'wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-22.04 -- bash -lc ...' on a script in simulation/scripts, from the Linux-side copy ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026 (Rebuild.bat runs 03_build.sh from the Windows folder to make that copy). The plugin turns Mission Planner, the ground station the team flies the real drone with, into the one ASTRA screen; it reads only MAVLink and uses WSL (simulation/scripts/mp_actions.sh) for its simulator buttons. The .bat files keep Windows CRLF line endings (.gitattributes).

mod:simulation/windows/Rebuild.bat.explain: Double-click after changing code: runs simulation/setup/03_build.sh inside Ubuntu-22.04, started from THIS Windows folder of the repo (wsl.exe --cd '<repo>'). 03_build.sh mirrors the repo to ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026 (photos and build results there are kept) and builds everything with colcon. The window says whether the build finished or failed (full log: ~/.astra_sim/logs/build_*.log inside Ubuntu) and waits for a key.
mod:simulation/windows/Rebuild.bat.how_it_fits: The Windows button for 'I edited the code, let the simulator use it'. The other launchers reuse the last build, so run this first after edits, and close the simulator first (Stop Simulation.bat): a running demo keeps the old build.

mod:simulation/windows/Start Over.bat.explain: Double-click: puts the running demo back to the start and flies it again. Inside Ubuntu-22.04 it runs 'bash simulation/scripts/start_over.sh --fly --follow' in the Linux-side copy. Gazebo and RViz stay open: a flying drone lands, a fresh drone with both payloads is placed, the autopilot and the team code restart, the mission is uploaded and flown, and this window shows every phase until the landing. With no simulator running it starts a fresh demo.
mod:simulation/windows/Start Over.bat.how_it_fits: The same as START OVER (twice) plus UPLOAD MISSION + START in the old demo panel, or START OVER in the Mission Planner plugin. It hands this repo's Windows folder to Ubuntu as ASTRA_WINDOWS_REPO (through WSLENV) and asks you to run Rebuild.bat first when the Linux copy does not exist yet.

mod:simulation/windows/Start Search Demo.explain: Double-click: the full search demo, kept open. Inside Ubuntu-22.04 it runs 'bash simulation/scripts/demo.sh runway --keep' from the Linux-side copy (the last build): the team's real flight code flies the search, finds the hiker and the tent, drops both payloads and lands, and then everything STAYS open for Start Over.bat (or START OVER) or Stop Simulation.bat.
mod:simulation/windows/Start Search Demo.how_it_fits: The quickest way to show the whole system on the team laptop. It passes ASTRA_WINDOWS_REPO through WSLENV so messages can name Windows paths, and reminds that Mission Planner can watch on UDP port 14550.

mod:simulation/windows/Start for Mission.explain: Double-click: the competition procedure in the simulator. Inside Ubuntu-22.04 it runs 'bash simulation/scripts/demo.sh runway --manual', which starts the simulator, the windows, the team's flight stack and the MAVLink copy for Mission Planner (UDP 14550), and then WAITS: you load, write, arm and start the mission in Mission Planner (the steps are printed). It shows the Windows path of the mission file to load (<repo>\ros2_ws\src\simulation\sim_worlds\missions\runway_survey.waypoints).
mod:simulation/windows/Start for Mission.how_it_fits: Practice for the real field: the human does what the pilot does in Mission Planner, the team's code does the rest. Everything stays open after the landing for another run (Start Over.bat or START OVER).

mod:simulation/windows/Stop Simulation.b.explain: Double-click: closes the simulator and everything it started. Inside Ubuntu-22.04 it runs 'bash simulation/scripts/stop_sim.sh' in the Linux-side copy, which stops only the simulator's own programs (found by their session tag), including the team stack that the demo or START OVER started. Mission Planner stays open; close it yourself.
mod:simulation/windows/Stop Simulation.b.how_it_fits: The Windows off switch. Safe to run twice; nothing else on the PC is touched.

mod:simulation/windows/check_mp_plugin.p.explain: Compiles the Mission Planner plugin (mission_planner_plugin\astra_gcs.cs) OUTSIDE Mission Planner, against Mission Planner's own program files (MissionPlanner.exe, MAVLink.dll, GMap.NET, ... in -MissionPlannerDir, default 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Mission Planner'), with the .NET Framework 4 C# compiler csc.exe (C# 5). A mistake then shows up with a line number instead of the plugin silently not appearing. The test DLL goes to the temp folder and is deleted; nothing is installed. Exit 0 = compiles, 1 = compile errors (printed), 2 = Mission Planner or the compiler not found.
mod:simulation/windows/check_mp_plugin.p.how_it_fits: A check to run before install_mp_plugin.ps1. The old .NET Framework compiler is stricter than Mission Planner's, so code that passes here also compiles inside Mission Planner.

mod:simulation/windows/install_mp_plugin.explain: Puts the ASTRA plugin into Mission Planner, or takes it out with -Remove. It finds MissionPlanner.exe (in -MissionPlannerDir, $env:MISSION_PLANNER_DIR, 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Mission Planner' or 'C:\Program Files\Mission Planner'), copies mission_planner_plugin\astra_gcs.cs to '<Mission Planner>\plugins\astra_gcs.cs' when the file hashes differ, and says to restart Mission Planner if it is open. Exit 0 = done, 1 = Mission Planner not found, 2 = the plugins folder is not writable (run once as administrator).
mod:simulation/windows/install_mp_plugin.how_it_fits: Mission Planner compiles every .cs file in its plugins folder when it starts, so installing means copying and restarting. sim_demo/mission_planner.py (behind mission_planner.sh start) does the same copy automatically before it opens Mission Planner.

pkg:simulation/windows/mission_planner_p.explain: The ASTRA Mission Planner plugin: one C# source file, astra_gcs.cs, which Mission Planner compiles by itself when it starts.
pkg:simulation/windows/mission_planner_p.how_it_fits: It replaces the old Qt demo panel: Mission Planner becomes the single ground-station screen for both the simulator and the real drone.

mod:simulation/windows/mission_planner_p.explain: The ASTRA Mission Planner plugin, version 1.1: it makes Mission Planner the ONE ground-station screen of the search mission (it replaces the old Qt demo panel, which demo.sh now leaves off unless --panel). It adds (1) the drone camera as the HUD background with no clicks (an MJPEG stream, default http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg from sim_demo's pov_server, which draws the gimbal angles on the picture); (2) an 'ASTRA' tab on the DATA screen, kept in FIRST place, with the mission phase strip, one plain sentence about what the drone is doing (or, when no telemetry came for more than 10 s, a plain warning that the numbers are old), 8 readouts, a card each for the hiker and the tent, an event log and buttons (ARM + START MISSION, RETURN HOME, and in the simulator TAKE PHOTO, CAMERA DOWN, CAMERA FORWARD, START OVER); and (3) map markers for the chosen targets and the drop points. Every 2 s it writes Documents\Mission Planner\astra_plugin_status.json.
mod:simulation/windows/mission_planner_p.how_it_fits: It learns everything from what Mission Planner already receives over MAVLink, so it works the same with the real drone over the telemetry radio: the autopilot's state, and the STATUSTEXT messages the team's main_controller sends through MAVROS ('Detected tent', 'All N images processed', 'Aim tent <lat>,<lon>', 'Targets: ...', 'Over tent:', 'Servo 13 -> 1400', 'RTL') plus the optional Lattice reporter's 'TGT p <lat> <lon> <conf> <n>'. Those texts reach Mission Planner because MAVROS talks to SITL SERIAL2 (TCP 5763), wired like the real Jetson on TELEM2. 'Detected ...' and 'All N images processed' come from the legacy (2025) photo pipeline (new_od and the photo hold), and the TAKE PHOTO button publishes /camera/trigger for the legacy video_cam node; with the new video pipeline (zr10_ros2 + zr10_stream + the detection package) the team has not decided yet which texts the mission sends, so those parts may stay quiet. Only the camera picture (HTTP) and the simulator buttons (wsl.exe running simulation/scripts/mp_actions.sh) use something else. Settings live in Mission Planner's config.xml (astra_camera_on, astra_camera_url, astra_sim_buttons, astra_wsl_distro, astra_wsl_repo, astra_drop_channels '11:person,13:tent', astra_drop_open_pwm 1400). Written for Mission Planner 1.3.83 in plain C# 5; check it with check_mp_plugin.ps1, install it with install_mp_plugin.ps1 (or mission_planner.sh start).

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: The mission phases in flight order, as the strip shows them from left to right: Waiting, Takeoff, Search, Process, Targets, Drop, Return, Landed.

Everything known about one target kind ('person' = the hiker, or 'tent'): how many 'Detected' messages came, when it was first seen, the best radio report (TGT) and its position, the chosen aim point, and whether its payload is dropping or dropped (with time and position).
The word used in sentences: 'hiker' for the person, 'tent' for the tent.
One line of the event log: time, source ('autopilot', 'flight code', 'Jetson report' or 'ASTRA'), text, and level (0 normal, 1 good news, 2 warning shown in amber).
The tab's colours, dark like Mission Planner's own theme: background, card, line, text, muted grey, accent blue, good green, warning amber, bad red, and a green fill and text for finished things.

Small helpers that make labels and set fonts WITHOUT naming the drawing types (Font, FontStyle, ContentAlignment) that Mission Planner ships twice (its own SkiaSharp-based copy and .NET's). Naming them would not compile, so these helpers reach them through reflection.
Gives a control the 'Segoe UI' font at a size, bold or regular. The font object is created by reflection and cached (one per size and style); on any error the control simply keeps its default font.
Centres a label's text by setting TextAlign to the value 32 (MiddleCenter) through reflection; if that fails the text stays left-aligned, which is fine too.
Makes a new label with a text, a text colour, a see-through background, '...' for text that does not fit, and the font from SetFont.
The row of 8 phase boxes at the top of the ASTRA tab: finished phases get a tick and a green fill, the current one is filled blue, the coming ones stay grey.
Builds the strip: one equal-width column per phase name (Waiting, Take-off, Search, Process, Targets, Drop, Return, Landed), each a centred bold label, and starts at phase 0 (Waiting).
The index of the current phase (0 = Waiting). Setting a new value re-colours every box: earlier ones ticked and green, this one blue, later ones grey.

The plugin itself, a Mission Planner 'Plugin'. It keeps the mission state (phase, targets, events) on Mission Planner's plugin thread, reads the camera stream on its own thread, and changes the ASTRA tab only on the window thread.
The plugin's name shown by Mission Planner: 'ASTRA ground station'.
The plugin's version, '1.1' (also written into the status file and the 'plugin loaded' line).
The author shown by Mission Planner: 'ASTRA team'.
Called once when Mission Planner loads the plugin: asks Mission Planner to call Loop 2 times per second (loopratehz = 2) and creates the two empty target records 'person' and 'tent'.

Called when Mission Planner's screens exist: builds the ASTRA tab, adds the 'ASTRA camera' HUD menu and the map layer, notes the load time (EnsureTab only selects the tab during the first 2 minutes after it), subscribes to every STATUSTEXT packet with TrySubscribe (Tick retries every 10 s if that failed), logs 'ASTRA ground station plugin 1.1 loaded', starts the camera thread and writes the first status file. Every part catches its own errors (kept in lastError), so one failure never stops the others or Mission Planner.
Called by Mission Planner 2 times per second: runs Tick and catches any error.
Called when Mission Planner closes: tells the camera thread to stop, removes the STATUSTEXT subscription and clears the camera picture from the HUD.

Runs on Mission Planner's MAVLink reader thread for every STATUSTEXT packet. It skips the autopilot's own texts (component 1; ReadMessages gets those), decodes the text and queues it with its 'sysid:compid' source, keeping at most 500 waiting. It stays fast: the parsing happens later in Tick.
Reads one value from Mission Planner's settings (config.xml), or returns the fallback when it is empty or cannot be read.
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.inputs: the setting's key and a fallback value

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: Stores one value in Mission Planner's settings (config.xml); errors are ignored.
True unless the setting astra_camera_on is 'false' (default 'true').
The camera stream address: the setting astra_camera_url, default http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg.

The update that runs 2 times per second. It reads new autopilot and companion status texts, decides whether this is the simulator, measures how old the telemetry is (TelemetryAge), retries the STATUSTEXT subscription every 10 s if it failed, every 2 s asks the window thread to put the ASTRA tab back in first place (EnsureTabAsync), notices arming (a new flight starts; after Landed the facts are reset) and disarming, and works out the phase: not armed = Waiting or Landed; RTL, LAND, SMART_RTL or a return message = Return; a drop under way or done = Drop; targets chosen = Targets; search done or photos processed = Process; AUTO above 10 m at waypoint 2 or later = Search; otherwise Takeoff. During a flight the phase never steps back. Then it writes the status file every 2 s and asks the window thread to redraw.

Decides whether the simulator buttons are shown: the setting astra_sim_buttons 'on' or 'off' wins; 'auto' (the default) means yes when the autopilot has the parameter SIM_SPEEDUP, which only SITL has.

Clears the facts of the last flight (search done, targets chosen, returning, photos processed, and each target's detections, report, aim and drop), marks the map for redrawing and logs '---- a new flight starts ----'.

Reads the newest status texts of the autopilot (component 1) from Mission Planner's message list, skips the ones already handled (Remember) and passes each new one to HandleText. Texts of other components arrive through OnStatusText instead, so nothing is counted twice.
Takes every text OnStatusText queued from the companion side (the Jetson's MAVROS or another component), counts it, and passes it to HandleText with its component id.
Remembers message ids (source, time and text) so every message is handled once; above 3000 it forgets the oldest. Returns false for a message it has seen before.

Turns one status text from the autopilot or the team's code into mission facts, by matching it against a few fixed patterns (listed under 'effects'). Texts with words like FAILED, timeout or PreArm are logged as warnings, and every text goes into the event log.
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.effects: 'Detected person|tent' counts a detection; 'TGT p|t <lat> <lon> <conf> <n>' keeps the best radio report; 'All N images processed' or 'Reached last WP' = search done; 'Aim person|tent <lat>,<lon>' = target position and map marker; 'Targets:' = targets chosen; 'Over person|tent:' = dropping; 'Servo <channel> -> <pwm>' = payload released when the channel is in astra_drop_channels and pwm equals the open value (1400), with the drone's position as the drop point; 'RTL', 'All targets done', 'No valid targets' or 'Divert failed' = returning

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: Reads the setting astra_drop_channels (default '11:person,13:tent') into a table: servo channel -> payload kind.
Reads the setting astra_drop_open_pwm: the servo value that means 'payload released' (default 1400 microseconds, the team's PULLEY_OPEN).

Adds one line to the event log (keeping the last 500) and to the list of lines the screen has not shown yet. There are two versions with the same name: one stamps the time 'now', the other uses the time of the message.

The camera thread's loop: when the camera is switched off it waits 1 s; when the stream's /health address does not answer it waits 2 s ('waiting for the camera stream'); otherwise it reads the stream (ReadStream) until it ends or fails, then clears the HUD picture, logs 'Camera picture off', waits 1 s and tries again, until Mission Planner closes.

Turns the stream address into its health address: it keeps 'http://host:port' and adds '/health' (http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg becomes http://127.0.0.1:8081/health, which sim_demo's pov_server answers).
Asks an address with one HTTP GET (1.5 s time limit, no proxy) and answers true only for status 200 OK.

Reads the MJPEG stream (pictures one after another over HTTP, 5 s silence limit), cuts out each complete JPEG (from the bytes FF D8 to FF D9; anything over 8 MB is thrown away) and shows it with ShowFrame, as long as the camera stays on and its address does not change.

Turns one JPEG into a .NET picture (Image.FromStream, found by reflection) and sets it as the HUD's background (FlightData.myhud.bgimage); it counts frames and disposes old pictures so only the newest 4 are kept.
Removes the camera picture from the HUD (bgimage = null), so Mission Planner's normal artificial horizon comes back, and disposes the pictures it kept.

Builds the ASTRA tab (named 'tabASTRA', so EnsureTab can find it) and puts it FIRST and selected on the DATA screen's tab row: the phase strip; the status sentence and link line; a 4 x 2 grid of readouts (MODE, HEIGHT, SPEED, BATTERY, GPS, HOME, IN THE AIR, WAYPOINT); the HIKER and TENT cards; the event log (Time, From, Message); the flight buttons; and the hidden row of simulator buttons.
Makes one readout tile: a small grey caption on top and a big value below ('-' at first), and remembers the value label under the caption's name.
Makes one target card (hiker or tent): a title, three text lines (detections, target, payload) and a coloured stripe on the left whose colour shows how far that target has come.
Makes one flat coloured button with white bold text, a given size and a click action.
Asks the window thread to run UpdateUi (BeginInvoke), because only that thread may change the screen; it does nothing before the tab exists.

Redraws the tab from the current state: the phase strip; the status sentence, or, when no telemetry came for more than 10 s, in amber 'No telemetry for <age>: the simulator or the radio link is off. The numbers below are the last ones received.'; the link line ('Telemetry live' below 5 s, 'Telemetry LOST (last packet <age> ago)', or when the age is unknown 'Telemetry connected' / 'No telemetry link', plus the camera state, the picture count and the seconds since the last message); the 8 readouts from Mission Planner's CurrentState (battery below 30 % and GPS without a 3D fix in red); both target cards and their colours; the newest event-log lines (at most 300 kept, newest on top); whether the simulator buttons are visible; and the map when it changed.
Changes a label's text only when it is different, so the screen does not flicker.
Sets one readout tile's value text and colour, found by its caption name.

Builds the plain sentence under the strip for the current phase, for example 'Searching: waypoint 5, 30 m, 5.5 m/s. Detections so far: hiker 2, tent 1', 'Over the tent: dropping the payload' or 'Returning home: 120 m to go, 30 m high'.
Adds a map layer named 'astra' to the flight-data map; the target and drop markers go there.
Redraws the map markers: a red (hiker) or orange (tent) dot with a label at each chosen target, and a small green marker at each payload release point.

Adds 'ASTRA camera' to the HUD's right-click menu: a tick box to show or hide the drone camera (setting astra_camera_on) and 'Camera address ...' to type another MJPEG address (setting astra_camera_url); the camera thread notices the change and reconnects.

The ARM + START MISSION button. It refuses when the drone has fewer than 2 mission items, asks 'Arm the motors and start the mission (AUTO)?', and then, in the background, sets GUIDED, waits 0.5 s, arms, waits 1 s and sets AUTO, logging each result (a refused arm is logged as a warning: see the PreArm messages).
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.effects: MAVLink mode and arm commands through Mission Planner's own functions (setMode, doARM)

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: The RETURN HOME (RTL) button: asks 'Fly back to the launch point and land (RTL)?' and then switches the autopilot to RTL in the background, logging the result.
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.effects: a MAVLink mode change to RTL

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: The simulator's START OVER button: explains what will happen (a flying drone lands, a fresh drone with both payloads stands at the start, the mission is uploaded again), asks for a yes, and runs the start_over action through RunSimAction.

Runs one simulator button in the background through WSL: wsl.exe -d <astra_wsl_distro, default Ubuntu-22.04> -- bash -lc 'bash <astra_wsl_repo>/simulation/scripts/mp_actions.sh <action>' (from a 32-bit process it uses Sysnative\wsl.exe), waits up to 15 minutes, and logs ': done' or ': FAILED' together with the script's last output line. TAKE PHOTO publishes /camera/trigger, which only the legacy (2025) photo pipeline's video_cam node listens to; CAMERA DOWN / FORWARD publish gimbal_set_angles on /camera/command (also a video_cam topic).
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.inputs: the action (take_photo, look_down, look_forward or start_over) and a label for the log
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.effects: starts a WSL process that publishes on /camera/trigger or /camera/command, or runs start_over.sh

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: Writes Documents\Mission Planner\astra_plugin_status.json: plugin version, time, phase, whether the tab was built, where the tab is (tab_index), whether it is selected, how often it was put back (tab_reinserts), how old the telemetry is (telemetry_age_s, null when unknown), camera state, picture count and age of the last picture, messages and companion texts seen, whether the STATUSTEXT subscription works, simulator yes/no, photos processed, each target's detections, target position and release time, the number of events, the last event and the last error. Tick calls it every 2 s, so scripts and teammates can check the plugin works without looking at the screen.
Adds one 'name: value' line to the status file's JSON text, either raw (numbers, true or false) or as a quoted string with backslashes, quotes and line breaks made safe.

pkg:simulation/profiles.explain: Plug-in profiles: small YAML files that say which piece fills each 'slot' of the simulator (world, autopilot, camera, detector, mission brain, extra programs, network addresses, run settings). A profile only holds the lines it changes; default.yaml writes every setting out. Use one with 'demo.sh --profile NAME' or 'start_sim.sh --profile NAME'.
pkg:simulation/profiles.how_it_fits: Read by sim_plugins.profile_tool (called by demo.sh and start_sim.sh only when --profile, --set or a plug-in option is given; otherwise the scripts run exactly as before and no profile is read). profile_tool merges the profile with default.yaml (and 'extends:'), checks every value and file, and turns it into sim.launch.py arguments, team-stack arguments and stack_check options. Simulator only: on the real drone a new detector must go into main/launch/tracker.launch.xml. AGENTS.md marks the plug-and-play mechanism as work in progress.

mod:simulation/profiles/README.md.explain: A short guide to the profiles folder: what a profile is, a table of every shipped profile and what it changes, and the commands to use one (demo.sh --profile ...) and to check one (python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool list / plan --profile X --check).
mod:simulation/profiles/README.md.how_it_fits: Points to docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md (every slot's contract and key) and docs/simulation/ARDUPILOT.md (the autopilot slot).

mod:simulation/profiles/default.yaml.explain: The profile that is EXACTLY today's simulator, with every setting written out and explained in a comment. The values: world runway with its own survey mission; autopilot sitl_binary (~/sitl/arducopter 4.6.3, instance 0, safe parameter filter); camera siyi_emulator, model zr10 (2560x1440 photos), zoom survey (full 81 degree view); detector team (new_od + ~/.astra_sim/models/yolo26m.pt, not batched); mission_brain team (main_controller.py); no extras; network: MAVProxy outputs on UDP 14550 (our scripts / a ground station), 14552 (MAVROS's old door) and 14553 (demo panel), windows_gcs true, camera_ip 192.168.144.25, and fcu_url '' = MAVROS on tcp://127.0.0.1:<5763 + 10 x instance> (SITL's SERIAL2, like the Jetson on TELEM2); run not headless, 30 minute timeout, team stack local.
mod:simulation/profiles/default.yaml.how_it_fits: The reference to copy when making your own profile (then delete every line you do not change). 'demo.sh --profile default' equals plain 'demo.sh'. sim_plugins' unit tests (test_profiles.py) check this file equals the built-in defaults.

mod:simulation/profiles/truth_detector.y.explain: Flies the demo with the ANSWER-KEY detector instead of the team's YOLO model: detector.kind truth, so sim_demo's truth_detector publishes the same /image_detection messages new_od would, for every photo that shows a target, using the world's truth file. The panel shows an amber 'STAND-IN' banner.
mod:simulation/profiles/truth_detector.y.how_it_fits: The same as 'demo.sh runway --detector truth'. Used to test the mission logic (waypoint insertion, drops, RTL) even when the real detector misses the simulated targets.

mod:simulation/profiles/example_detector.explain: Plugs the TEMPLATE detector (sim_plugin_examples/example_detector, a colour-blob finder) into the demo in place of the team's new_od: detector.kind custom with package example_detector, launch file example_detector.launch.py, node name example_detector, provides_health true and the launch argument min_blob_area_px 150.
mod:simulation/profiles/example_detector.how_it_fits: team_stack.launch.py then starts a copy of tracker.launch.xml WITHOUT new_od plus this detector; stack_check waits for the node example_detector and its /sahi/get_health 'ModelLoaded: True' answer. Copy it next to your own detector package and change the package, launch and node_name lines; check it while it runs with 'ros2 run sim_plugins check_slot --slot detector --take-photo'.

mod:simulation/profiles/example_listener.explain: Starts the TEMPLATE 'extra' (sim_plugin_examples/example_listener) together with the team stack: a node that only LISTENS (telemetry, mission progress, detections), prints a summary every 10 s (summary_period_s) and writes a JSON summary file when it stops (default ~/.astra_sim/example_listener_summary.json).
mod:simulation/profiles/example_listener.how_it_fits: Shows how 'extras' add a logger, monitor or test driver without touching anything else; start_with team_stack starts it with ./launcher.sh sim (start_with simulator would start it with sim.launch.py). Another profile can say 'extends: example_listener'.

mod:simulation/profiles/lattice_mock.yam.explain: Tries the Lattice bridge with the simulated drone and NO Lattice account. It adds four extra programs to the normal demo: lattice_ground_radio (a second ground station that plays the field's telemetry radio), fake_lattice (a pretend Lattice with a live map at http://127.0.0.1:8089/), lattice_bridge (the real ground-side bridge, publishing to the pretend Lattice) and lattice_reporter (the Jetson-side reporter that sends one short text such as 'TGT p 36.215133 -96.006219 95 1' per hiker or tent through MAVROS).
mod:simulation/profiles/lattice_mock.yam.effects: lattice_ground_radio = MAVProxy on the autopilot's spare port SERIAL1 (TCP 5762, system id 254), started by sim_bringup's wait_then_exec once that port listens, output UDP 14554, log <run folder>/lattice/lattice_ground_radio.tlog; fake_lattice journal <run folder>/lattice/fake_lattice_journal.jsonl, answering 4 s past the end; lattice_bridge reads udpin:127.0.0.1:14554 with a made-up token; lattice_reporter starts with the team stack with min_confidence 0.5 and min_move_m 1.5
mod:simulation/profiles/lattice_mock.yam.how_it_fits: Since 2026-10-31 the Lattice work belongs to the TEAM: the owner stopped the AI-assisted work and handed it over in commit f139036; the team continues from docs/lattice/HANDOFF.md. The team's target and drop texts ('TGT ...', 'Servo 13 -> 1400') come through MAVROS; ArduPilot passes them on to every OTHER port where it heard a ground station, so the ground station on SERIAL1 receives them the way the real radio does (MAVProxy never copies one client's messages to another). The file (unchanged since f139036) still pins network.fcu_url udp://:14552@localhost:14552 (MAVROS behind MAVProxy) instead of the SERIAL2 default, so during this demo Mission Planner gets none of the team's texts. Its stated reason, mission_tool reading MAVROS's heartbeat as 'STABILIZE, disarmed', was fixed in commit 9ef3c01 (mission_tool now reads the drone's state from the autopilot component only); simplifying the profile (delete fcu_url and the second ground station, give the bridge a plain MAVProxy output) is step 3 of the team's hand-over list in docs/lattice/HANDOFF.md. Keep TCP 5762 free during this demo. Nothing leaves the computer and the flight is not affected if a part fails. Use: demo.sh runway --profile lattice_mock, then open http://127.0.0.1:8089/ (docs/lattice/BRIDGE.md).

mod:simulation/profiles/ardupilot_versio.explain: Flies the simulated drone with ANOTHER ArduCopter version than the real Pixhawk's 4.6.3: autopilot sitl_binary, version '4.7.1' (a folder in ~/sitl/versions, fetched first with 'bash simulation/setup/fetch_sitl.sh 4.7.1').
mod:simulation/profiles/ardupilot_versio.how_it_fits: Checks the team's code against a newer firmware before the drone is updated. That version keeps its own saved parameters in ~/.astra_sim/sitl_I0_v4.7.1, so the default's are not touched. Without editing: demo.sh --sitl-version latest.

mod:simulation/profiles/ardupilot_source.explain: Flies the simulated drone with ArduCopter BUILT FROM AN ARDUPILOT SOURCE TREE: autopilot sitl_source, source_dir /opt/ardupilot (the Docker 'sitl' image's Copter-4.6.3 build), whose build/sitl/bin/arducopter and own Tools/autotest/default_params files are used.
mod:simulation/profiles/ardupilot_source.how_it_fits: For trying firmware changes: build a tree once (./waf configure --board sitl && ./waf copter), then demo.sh --profile ardupilot_source, or demo.sh --sitl-source ~/ardupilot for your own tree (docs/simulation/ARDUPILOT.md).

mod:simulation/profiles/real_drone_param.explain: Makes the simulated autopilot fly the mission like the REAL drone by loading the real Pixhawk's parameter file on top of the simulator's own: autopilot.param_files [params/example_real_drone.param] (a path relative to this profile's folder) with param_filter safe and an empty param_keep list.
mod:simulation/profiles/real_drone_param.how_it_fits: The 'safe' filter keeps lines about how the drone flies the mission (waypoint speed and radius, RTL height, failsafes) and drops lines about the PHYSICAL drone that would break the simulator (sensor calibrations, wiring, airframe and tuning, the payload servos). The plan says how many lines were used and dropped: python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool plan --profile real_drone_params --check. Quick way: demo.sh --param-file <file>.

mod:simulation/profiles/external_autopil.explain: EXAMPLE with made-up addresses: the autopilot runs SOMEWHERE ELSE (another container or PC) and this computer runs Gazebo, MAVProxy, the camera emulator and the demo. autopilot kind external, mavlink tcp:192.168.1.50:5760 (where that SITL's MAVLink is), fdm_addr 0.0.0.0 (the drone plugin here listens for physics on every address) and sim_address 192.168.1.20 (this computer, for the printed command).
mod:simulation/profiles/external_autopil.how_it_fits: On the other computer SITL runs 'arducopter --model JSON --sim-address=<this PC> ...' and sends its physics packets to UDP 9002 here; MAVProxy here connects to its TCP 5760 and shares the MAVLink out as usual. Firewalls must open UDP 9002 here and TCP 5760 there.

mod:simulation/profiles/docker_split.yam.explain: EXAMPLE network settings for a split setup: this container or PC runs the simulator, and the team stack (./launcher.sh sim) runs in ANOTHER container, like on the real drone's Jetson. network.mavros_out udp:172.30.0.3:14552 (change to the other container's address), camera_bind 0.0.0.0 (the camera emulator answers on every address), windows_gcs false; run.team_stack external (demo.sh does not start launcher.sh, it waits for it) and headless true.
mod:simulation/profiles/docker_split.yam.how_it_fits: On the other side MAVROS must listen on every address (FCU_URL='udp://:14552@' ./launcher.sh sim), this side needs the camera address 192.168.144.25 on the shared Docker network, and both need the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID and working ROS 2 discovery. docker/compose.sim.yml is the ready-made version of this idea.

pkg:simulation/profiles/params.explain: Example parameter files for profiles (today one file, example_real_drone.param).
pkg:simulation/profiles/params.how_it_fits: Referenced by real_drone_params.yaml through a path relative to the profiles folder.

mod:simulation/profiles/params/example_r.explain: A SHORT EXAMPLE of a parameter file saved from Mission Planner (CONFIG -> Full Parameter List -> Save to file), one NAME,VALUE per line. The first block describes how the drone flies the mission (WPNAV_SPEED 500, WPNAV_RADIUS 200, RTL_ALT 3000, LAND_SPEED 50, failsafes ...), which the simulator uses; the second block describes the physical drone (sensor offsets, compass, serial ports, battery, frame, motor and rate tuning, SERVO11/13_FUNCTION, SYSID_THISMAV ...), which the 'safe' filter drops.
mod:simulation/profiles/params/example_r.how_it_fits: Used by real_drone_params.yaml to show how the filter works. It is NOT the real drone's parameter list: replace it with yours.

pkg:..explain: The repository root. It holds launcher.sh (the entry point of the team's flight software), the guides (README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md), the Jetson's pip pins (requirements_jetson.txt and its .lock), ruff.toml (lint rules), saved Lattice SDK pages and team notes. An empty COLCON_IGNORE file keeps colcon out of it: ROS packages are built inside ros2_ws.
pkg:..how_it_fits: Everything hangs below it: ros2_ws/ (team and simulation ROS 2 packages), simulation/ (the simulator's scripts, profiles, Docker helpers and Windows launchers), docker/ (images and compose files), scripts/ (operator tools) and docs/. Two loose bench files also sit here: servo_wiggle.py (swings servo output 13 with pymavlink, like the tools in servo_test/) and its stray copy servo_wiggle.py'.

mod:launcher.sh.bak.explain: The OLD launcher, kept as a backup copy: it sources ROS 2 Humble and the workspace, starts MAVROS with px4.launch (the PX4 settings, not ArduPilot's) on FCU_URL (default /dev/ttyUSB0:115200), waits up to 30 s for /mavros/state, then runs 'ros2 launch main tracker.launch.xml' in the foreground.
mod:launcher.sh.bak.how_it_fits: DEAD (AGENTS.md): replaced by launcher.sh (apm.launch, sim mode, readable logs, camera ping, TRACKER_CMD). Nothing calls it.

mod:simulation/docker/check_host.sh.explain: The Docker 'doctor': checks whether THIS computer is ready for the ASTRA containers, in the order a first run meets the problems, and for every problem prints what is wrong and exactly what to type to fix it. It changes nothing (only --fix-line-endings rewrites line ends, and --deep starts small test containers). Exit code 0 = nothing blocks Docker (warnings may remain), 1 = at least one [FAIL] to fix first.
mod:simulation/docker/check_host.sh.outputs: a report in 7 sections (8 with --deep): 1 the computer (WSL2 or Linux, not root, x86_64, Ubuntu 22.04, about 8 GB memory); 2 the repo copy (Linux-side copy up to date, Windows CRLF line endings in scripts, root-owned folders); 3 Docker (installed, the right program, allowed, running, buildx, Compose 2.20+, credential helpers, disk space, compose files valid, leftover containers and networks, subnet 192.168.144.0/24 free); 4 the images (built, not running as root, up to date, your user id); 5 internet, proxy and clock; 6 windows, 3D and the NVIDIA card; 7 things in the way (a native simulator, busy ports, the camera address, detector weights); 8 test containers (images' self-test, name lookup, GPU).
mod:simulation/docker/check_host.sh.how_it_fits: Run before a first Docker build or when a container run fails. It uses _host_common.sh's helpers (astra_copy_differences, astra_compose_files, astra_subnet_conflict, astra_image_label, astra_docker_inputs_hash, astra_free_gb, astra_native_sim_running ...) and, with --deep, build_images.sh --check. Options: --offline, --deep, --fix-line-endings, --repo DIR. Its header points to check_host.ps1 for the Windows side (the PowerShell half of the doctor, added on 2026-10-31) and to docs/simulation/DOCKER.md 'Troubleshooting'.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::pass.explain: Prints a '[ OK ]' line: this check passed.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::note.explain: Prints a '[ .. ]' line: a fact worth knowing that is not a problem.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::caut.explain: Prints a '[WARN]' line and adds 1 to the warnings counter: something that may cause trouble but does not block Docker.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::fail.explain: Prints a '[FAIL]' line and adds 1 to the failures counter; any failure makes the script end with exit code 1. (This is check_host.sh's own report helper, not a stop like fetch_sitl.sh's fail.)

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::tip.explain: Prints an indented '-> ...' line with the exact fix for the finding just above.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::titl.explain: Prints an empty line and a section title such as '3. Docker'.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::fix_.explain: Repairs scripts that a Windows git clone (core.autocrlf=true) gave Windows line endings: for every file that git stores with LF but finds with CRLF (or mixed) on disk, it removes the CR characters with sed. Files marked eol=crlf (Windows .bat, .cmd, .ps1) keep CRLF and symbolic links are skipped. Then it runs 'git add' on exactly the repaired files whose content now equals git's copy, so git stops listing them as modified (files with your own edits stay modified), and it reminds you to refresh the Linux-side copy.
fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::fix_.inputs: the checkout folder (must be a git checkout)
fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::fix_.effects: rewrites the line ends of the affected files; refreshes git's index entry of the repaired files that are otherwise unchanged (nothing new is staged)

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::net_.explain: Tries all 14 download sites the image build and the first run need (Docker Hub, packages.ros.org, snapshots.ros.org, keyserver.ubuntu.com, archive.ubuntu.com, packages.osrfoundation.org, GitHub and its file servers, PyPI, download.pytorch.org, SourceForge, fuel.gazebosim.org) at the same time with curl (8 s each, through this terminal's proxy). Unreachable sites go into NET_BAD; sites that answer with a certificate this Linux does not trust (a network that inspects HTTPS) go into NET_TLS.
fn:simulation/docker/check_host.sh::net_.called_when: section 5, unless --offline, curl is missing or name lookup already fails

mod:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1.explain: The WINDOWS half of the Docker 'doctor' (check_host.sh is the Linux half), run in PowerShell before a teammate's first Docker build on Windows. It checks what only Windows can see: the Windows build, virtualization in the BIOS, how much memory WSL gets (.wslconfig; about 8 GB is needed), free space on the drive of the Ubuntu-22.04 virtual disk, WSL and the Ubuntu-22.04 distro (installed, WSL version 2, the default distro), Docker Desktop and its WSL integration, Windows line endings (CRLF) in this checkout's scripts, OneDrive and long paths, the NVIDIA driver, who listens on UDP 14550, a proxy, and (unless -Offline) internet access to github.com and the clock. It changes nothing; every problem is printed with exactly what to do, and the exit code is 0 (nothing on the Windows side blocks Docker) or 1 (a [FAIL] to fix first).
mod:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1.how_it_fits: Run from the repository folder with 'powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File simulation\docker\check_host.ps1' (add -Offline to skip the internet check); the next step is check_host.sh inside Ubuntu ('wsl -d Ubuntu-22.04'), which can also repair CRLF scripts with --fix-line-endings. Every message is explained in docs/simulation/DOCKER.md, 'Troubleshooting'. New on 2026-10-31 (described as it was on disk then).

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Pas.explain: Prints a '[ OK ]' line: this check passed.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Not.explain: Prints a '[ .. ]' line: a fact worth knowing that is not a problem.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Cau.explain: Prints a '[WARN]' line and adds 1 to the warning counter: something that may cause trouble but does not block Docker.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Fai.explain: Prints a '[FAIL]' line and adds 1 to the failure counter; any failure makes the script end with exit code 1.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Tip.explain: Prints an indented '-> ...' line with the exact fix for the finding just above it.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Tit.explain: Prints an empty line and then a section title such as '3. Docker on Windows'.

fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Fre.explain: Returns the free space, in whole gigabytes, of the drive that holds a folder (found from its drive letter with Get-PSDrive), or -1 when that cannot be found.
fn:simulation/docker/check_host.ps1::Fre.called_when: for the drive of the Ubuntu-22.04 virtual disk and of Docker Desktop's disk (a warning below 40 GB)

fn:simulation/docker/_host_common.sh::as.explain: Prints the user id build_images.sh builds into the images for THIS user, by the same rule: your own id when your user id AND group id are both 1000 or more (normal accounts), otherwise 1000, the Dockerfile's default (small ids such as 20 or 500 belong to system groups inside the Ubuntu image and would clash).
fn:simulation/docker/_host_common.sh::as.called_when: by astra_check_image_user and check_host.sh, to tell whether a rebuild would change anything

fn:simulation/docker/_host_common.sh::as.explain: Reads rsync's --itemize-changes list (lines like '>f+++++++++ path/to/file') and prints how many FILES would be copied, not counting tool caches (.ruff_cache, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .hypothesis ...) and editor/agent folders (.vscode, .claude). Those change all the time but never change what the containers run, so they must not set off the 'the Linux-side copy is OLDER' warning.
Turns an IPv4 address A.B.C.D into one whole number (A x 2^24 + B x 2^16 + C x 2^8 + D), so subnets can be compared with simple arithmetic in bash.

True when a network written as A.B.C.D/N (a bare address counts as /32) shares at least one address with the drone network 192.168.144.0/24 (ASTRA_SUBNET), in either direction: 192.168.144.25/32 (inside it) and 192.168.128.0/17 or 192.168.144.0/20 (around it) overlap; 192.168.145.0/24, IPv6 addresses and junk do not. It compares both addresses under the shorter of the two masks.

Prints a route of this computer that is WIDER than the drone network and covers it (for example '192.168.0.0/16 dev tun0', a VPN), or nothing. The containers still start (the Docker network's own /24 route is more exact and wins), but while they run this computer cannot reach the 192.168.144.x part of that wider network. Docker's own bridges (br-...) and the default route are ignored.
fn:simulation/docker/_host_common.sh::as.called_when: by check_host.sh section 3 (a warning, not a failure)

mod:.devcontainer/devcontainer.json.explain: The VS Code 'Reopen in Container' set-up of the team's normal development container, 'ASTRA ODLC dev': VS Code builds docker/Dockerfile's 'dev' target itself, mounts the repo, works as the user ubuntu, sends windows to an X server on the host (DISPLAY=host.docker.internal:0.0), gives ROS 2 1 GB of shared memory, keeps the bash history and the ccache in Docker volumes, and adds the C++, CMake, Python and Ruff extensions.
mod:.devcontainer/devcontainer.json.how_it_fits: The team's own dev container, unchanged by the simulator work; VS Code asks whether to open it or the simulator one (.devcontainer/sim/devcontainer.json). It has no header comment of its own.

mod:.devcontainer/sim/devcontainer.json.explain: The VS Code 'Reopen in Container' set-up for the SIMULATOR image astra-sim ('ASTRA simulator (Gazebo + SITL)'): Gazebo, RViz and the windows open on the Windows desktop through WSLg and draw with the graphics card (/dev/dxg, Mesa d3d12; CUDA when the NVIDIA toolkit is there), the camera address can be added inside (NET_ADMIN), and the colcon build goes into the same Docker volumes as the compose 'sim' container and run_sim_container.sh. Before starting (initializeCommand) it stops with a clear message when the image is not built yet (require_image.sh) and creates ~/.astra_docker and, since 2026-10-31, ros2_ws/build, install and log, which Docker would otherwise create owned by root.
mod:.devcontainer/sim/devcontainer.json.how_it_fits: The image is built by simulation/docker/build_images.sh sim (no login needed). Problems before the container starts: run simulation/docker/check_host.sh (docs/simulation/DOCKER.md). On a Linux desktop the WSLg lines are swapped for --device=/dev/dri (or use run_sim_container.sh).

pkg:.devcontainer.explain: VS Code's dev container settings: devcontainer.json (the team's normal 'dev' container) and sim/devcontainer.json (the simulator image astra-sim). VS Code asks which one to open.

mod:.gitattributes.explain: Git's line-ending rules for this repo (rewritten on 2026-10-31, commit 0e49505): every text file is checked out with Linux (LF) line ends on every computer, also on Windows where Git for Windows defaults to core.autocrlf=true; the Windows launchers (.bat, .cmd, .ps1) keep Windows (CRLF) line ends; pictures, PDFs and model weights are never converted; .devcontainer files keep 'merge=ours'. Files committed with CRLF stay as they are (text=auto), so nobody sees surprise changes.
mod:.gitattributes.how_it_fits: Why: a hidden carriage return breaks bash scripts ($'\r': command not found) and '#!/usr/bin/env python3' lines. An older Windows clone keeps its CRLF files until rewritten: simulation/docker/check_host.sh finds them and --fix-line-endings repairs them; simulation/docker/test/test_line_endings.py guards the rules.

fn:simulation/docker/test/test_check_hos.explain: Test helper: runs git in a folder quietly (the test fails on an error) and returns its output.

Test fixture: a temporary home folder and data folder, stand-in 'docker' and 'ip' commands on PATH (their answers set by STUB_* variables), and a small git checkout with LF files and ros2_ws/src, so check_host.sh can be run without Docker; skipped when git is missing.
Test helper: the fingerprint build_images.sh would store for this repo's docker/ files (astra_docker_inputs_hash from _host_common.sh), to make a stand-in image look up to date or stale.
Test helper: runs check_host.sh on the sandbox checkout with extra STUB_* settings for the stand-in commands and returns (exit code, all output).
Test helper: the lines of the doctor's output that contain '[FAIL]'.
Test helper: the files 'git status' shows as modified in the working tree, to prove --fix-line-endings leaves no surprise changes.
Test helper: runs a piece of bash with _host_common.sh loaded and returns its output (used for the subnet arithmetic, the copy-change counter and the user-id checks).

fn:simulation/docker/test/test_line_endi.explain: Test helper: runs git in the repository and returns its output; skips the test when git or a usable checkout is missing.
Test helper: the 'text' and 'eol' attributes git gives a path (git check-attr), as a small dictionary.

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: Subscribes to every STATUSTEXT packet from any system and component (0, 0 = all) with Mission Planner's SubscribeToPacketType, so the team code's texts, which arrive from MAVROS as component 191 and which Mission Planner files under that component instead of the autopilot, still reach OnStatusText. It notes the time of the try; a negative answer or an error is kept in the status file as '... (will retry)'.
fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.called_when: once from Loaded, then from Tick every 10 s while there is no subscription

fn:simulation/windows/mission_planner_pl.explain: How many seconds ago Mission Planner got the last good MAVLink packet from the drone (MAV.lastvalidpacket), or -1 when it never got one or the clocks look confused (more than 5 s in the future or more than 6 hours old). Needed because with a UDP connection Mission Planner keeps showing the last values ('Ready to Arm', 'GPS: rtk Fixed') after the simulator or the radio stopped.

Writes an age for people: below 120 seconds as whole seconds ('45 s'), otherwise as whole minutes ('7 min'). Used in the 'No telemetry for ...' sentence and the 'Telemetry LOST (last packet ... ago)' link line.
Asks the window thread to run EnsureTab (BeginInvoke), because only that thread may change the screen; it does nothing before the DATA screen and the tab exist.

Keeps the ASTRA tab in first place. Mission Planner rebuilds the DATA screen's tabs from its saved list ('tabcontrolactions' in config.xml) when the screen loads and after 'Customize', and drops tabs it does not know, such as this one. When the tab is missing or moved it is put back at position 0. It is selected only during the first 2 minutes after loading and only if Mission Planner just fell back to its default first tab ('Quick'), or if it was already selected; otherwise the pilot's own choice of tab is restored. The first time this happens it logs 'Mission Planner rebuilt its tabs: the ASTRA tab is back in first place'. Where the tab is, whether it is selected and how often it was put back go into the status file.
